title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
summary: ReAct presents an approach that interleaves reasoning traces with actions, giving an agent a repeated reason-act-observe pattern while interacting with tasks and environments.
key_points: Alternates internal reasoning with external actions.
Makes observations from actions part of the next decision step.
Provides a useful conceptual foundation for bounded agent loops.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK
summary: The OpenAI Agents SDK provides primitives for agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, and tracing, with an emphasis on a relatively small set of composable building blocks.
key_points: Supports tool-using agents and handoffs between specialized agents.
Includes guardrail and tracing concepts.
Uses application code to orchestrate agent behavior and state.

title: LangGraph
summary: LangGraph models agent workflows as stateful graphs. It emphasizes explicit state, durable execution, controlled workflow transitions, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
key_points: Represents workflows using graph nodes and transitions.
Makes state a first-class part of the application.
Targets long-running and controllable agent workflows.

title: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
summary: Google ADK is a development kit for building agent applications with tools, workflow agents, multi-agent composition, sessions, and model integrations.
key_points: Supports tool use and structured agent workflows.
Includes multi-agent composition patterns.
Provides session and state-oriented building blocks.

title: Microsoft Agent Framework
summary: Microsoft Agent Framework provides agent and workflow abstractions for building AI applications, including tool use, orchestration, stateful workflows, and multi-agent patterns.
key_points: Combines agent abstractions with workflow orchestration.
Supports tool-enabled and multi-agent application patterns.
Targets production-oriented application development.

title: Pydantic AI
summary: Pydantic AI is a Python agent framework that emphasizes typed application code, structured outputs, dependency injection, tool definitions, testing, and observability-friendly development.
key_points: Uses Python typing and Pydantic models heavily.
Supports tools and structured model outputs.
Places strong emphasis on testable application code.

title: CrewAI
summary: CrewAI focuses on organizing multiple role-oriented agents into crews and flows, providing abstractions for collaboration, delegation, tasks, and process-oriented orchestration.
key_points: Uses role-oriented agent abstractions.
Supports coordinated multi-agent workflows.
Emphasizes tasks, crews, and flows as orchestration concepts.

title: Model Context Protocol Specification
summary: The Model Context Protocol defines a standard way for AI applications to connect with tools, resources, and contextual capabilities through client-server interactions.
key_points: Separates AI applications from external capability providers.
Defines tools and resources as protocol-level concepts.
Introduces explicit trust and capability boundaries.

title: Demystifying Evals for AI Agents
summary: Agent evaluation guidance emphasizes defining tasks and outcomes, building representative evaluation cases, examining trajectories and failures, and measuring agent behavior rather than relying on isolated demos.
key_points: Evaluation should reflect realistic task success and failure modes.
Agent trajectories and intermediate behavior matter.
Regression-oriented evaluation is important for production reliability.
